Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv:2405.21075.
creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun (Nanjing University, State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, XMU, HKU, PKU, CUHK, ECNU, CASIA)
description: Video-MME is the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. It comprises 900 manually curated videos spanning 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, annotated with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice QA pairs (3 per video). Videos range from 11 seconds to 1 hour in duration, and the benchmark integrates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audios to enable comprehensive evaluation of MLLMs' video understanding capabilities.
name: Video-MME
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning. Additional contributors named in acknowledgments: Yu Bai, Fangyuan Liu, Yigeng Jiang, and Zezhong Wu.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement. The distribution of answer options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then iteratively created three relevant multiple-choice questions, each with four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. A quality review process followed: each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify (i) clear and precise language expression; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options and the correct answer is appropriate. Additionally, text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content; questions not meeting this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed to mitigate answer bias: the distribution of answer options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%). Videos were sourced from YouTube with a relatively balanced distribution of video durations across the 30 categories. The multilingual category is included to cover non-English content. The benchmark includes a quality filter using Gemini 1.5 Pro to prevent questions answerable from text alone (prior-knowledge bias).
rai:dataCollection: Videos were manually collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. For each category, videos were collected with varying duration lengths: short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes). Corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios were also obtained. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, 744 with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos sourced from YouTube spanning 6 visual domains and 30 fine-grained categories, along with their associated subtitles (if provided by the platform) and audio tracks.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reveals that all current MLLMs show a decline in performance as video duration increases, suggesting limitations in processing longer video sequences. Open-source models are limited by fixed numbers of input frames (e.g., 8 frames), resulting in excessively sparse information density for long videos. The benchmark highlights counting problems as a joint bottleneck for current multimodal models in video understanding.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were categorized into short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes) duration groups. Subtitles and audio tracks were extracted alongside videos. QA pairs that could be answered without video content (as determined by Gemini 1.5 Pro text-only evaluation achieving <15% accuracy threshold) were filtered out and revised.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Video-MME is intended to advance research toward artificial general intelligence by providing a comprehensive evaluation framework for MLLMs on video understanding. The benchmark highlights the need for improvements in handling longer multimodal sequences, which could inspire future MLLM development toward more capable and robust systems for real-world video analysis.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating and benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on video understanding tasks, including both image-based and video-based MLLMs. The benchmark is designed to assess capabilities across diverse video types, temporal durations, and multimodal inputs (frames, subtitles, audios), enabling comprehensive evaluation of temporal understanding, perception, reasoning, and information synthesis.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used during quality review to filter out QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions (without video content), ensuring questions require video as a critical clue.
